newsitem.title: MALAWI: U.N. disaster team assesses Malawi flood damage.
newsitem.headline: U.N. disaster team assesses Malawi flood damage.

text.p: A four-member team from the United Nations' Disaster Assessment and Coordination unit arrived in Malawi on Thursday to help assess damage to two flood-hit areas.

Malawi President Bakili Muluzi last week declared Chikwawa and Nsanje districts disaster areas and appealed for international aid to help the more than 80,000 people displaced by the floods. Among the homeless are 20,000 Mozambicans who crossed the Shire river into Malawi to avoid rising floodwaters.
In the meantime, the U.N's humanitarian agency has provided an emergency grant of $30,000 for the local purchase of relief items to cover the immediate needs of victims, a U.N. spokesman said.

"We are also in contact with our headquarters to secure some quick funding towards emergency relief and all U.N. agencies operating in the country are in regular contact to come up with a coordinated effort," acting resident representative for U.N. Development Programme in Malawi, El-Mostafa Benlamlih, said in a statement.
